# Best rechargeable AA batteries

**Best overall: Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA (2550 mAh).** Digital Camera World's top pick. The reviewer has used them for years in flash testing with "100 per cent reliability." They hold about 85% charge after a year and come pre-charged, but are rated for only about 500 recharges ([Digital Camera World](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)). GearLab also picks them for high-drain devices like cameras and game controllers, but lists them at about $17.99 per 4-pack ([GearLab](https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/)). Retailer buy buttons (Adorama, Amazon, Newegg, Best Buy) are on the [Digital Camera World guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries). I don't have a direct product URL, so check the current price there.

**Best for longevity: standard Panasonic Eneloop AA (2000 mAh).** It has lower capacity per charge, but it's rated for about 2,100 recharges and keeps 70% of its charge after 10 years in storage ([Digital Camera World](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)). It's a good fit for remotes, controllers and anything you recharge often.

**Best budget: IKEA LADDA.** Charge-Test measured the LADDA 2450 mAh at about 2,450 mAh at low load and about 2,350 mAh at 1A, essentially matching the Eneloop Pro. The reviewer concluded they remain "Eneloop-class cells at budget prices." IKEA has never confirmed who makes them, though ([Charge-Test](https://charge-test.com/ikea-ladda-batteries-review-still-the-best-budget-aa-aaa-rechargeable-in-2026/)). Two caveats:
- That test was done in Europe at €7.99 per 4-pack. The only US listing I found is the 1900 mAh version at $9.99 per 4-pack, comparable to the standard Eneloop: [IKEA US LADDA AA 1900mAh](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/). I couldn't confirm the 2450 mAh version is sold in the US, so check in-store.
- GearLab's $7.99 price for the 2450 mAh version isn't confirmed by IKEA's US page.

**Best for bulk buying: Tenergy Premium PRO AA (2800 mAh).** The 20-pack is $42.99 (about $2.15 per cell), with a claimed 85% charge retention after a year and 1,200 cycles. Those are manufacturer figures, not independent tests. The cells are 1.2V, so a few devices designed strictly for 1.5V may read them as low. [Buy the 20-pack at Tenergy](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack) (affiliate link; the price was verified 2026-10-21 and the warranty is listed as 12 months on the product page but 90 days on Tenergy's warranty page).

**For devices that need a true 1.5V:** Digital Camera World recommends the EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA (3000 mWh). It's the better choice if your gear misbehaves on 1.2V NiMH cells ([Digital Camera World](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)).

## Caveats
- **Be wary of the two Frame & Focal articles.** Their numbers conflict with other sources. One lists Eneloop Pro at 2,100 mAh and the other at 2,550, and they describe zinc dendrites in NiMH cells, which doesn't make chemical sense. I didn't base any picks on them.
- **Amazon Basics High-Capacity** gets mixed treatment. GearLab suggests it only for low-drain devices like clocks and remotes. I'd skip it for cameras and flashlights.

**Quick recommendation:** Get Eneloop Pro for high-drain gear, LADDA if you're near an IKEA and want to save, and standard Eneloop for low-drain devices you recharge constantly. You'll also need a charger, and IKEA sells the STENKOL for $8.99.
